title: Read and manage existing todos
summary: List, search, or inspect Todo records; decide pending concern-routing proposals; add notes; and mark a todo done or reopen it.
use_when: An existing concern, routing proposal, durable umbrella, direction history, note, lifecycle state, assessment, or design projection should be read.
A person has explicitly authorized a routing decision or an umbrella note/open-done transition.
do_not_use_when: A new concern should be captured and researched.
The task is to implement, plan, or prove completion of the underlying work.
A routing proposal's frozen basis is stale or authorization provenance is unavailable.
outcome: An exact Todo read or deterministic provenance-bearing identity, note, or lifecycle transition, without model authority or implementation claims.
effects: List, search, and show commands read Todo state without invoking Nucleus.
Routing accept/reject records an explicit decision using a readable UTF-8 source as authorization provenance.
Note add appends an immutable working note; done and reopen perform idempotent umbrella lifecycle transitions.
authority: Todo owns concern and umbrella identities, direction revisions, notes, routing decisions, lifecycle, assessments, and design projections.
Only deterministic CLI decision commands, not a model job or final prose, authorize routing.
success: Reads identify the exact public ID and current or historical state selected.
Routing acceptance applies a still-pending proposal whose complete frozen basis remains current.
Lifecycle and note writes are durably visible without being misrepresented as implementation execution.
failure_and_recovery: There is no force option for stale routing; reassess the original concern.
An attachment does not revise direction, a revision does not merge identities, and unification preserves superseded history.
Done/reopen does not prove that any particular plan ran; inspect external state separately.
privacy: Todo reads can expose source paths, directions, notes, assessment evidence references, and design content.
Decision sources must be readable UTF-8 at decision time; Todo stores their canonical paths, not contents.
does_not_authorize: Implementation or execution of the todo direction.
Inferring completion evidence from an open/done marker.
A routing decision without explicit readable decision-source provenance.

consumers.statement: A current-user caller may inspect exact Todo identities and history or perform an explicitly authorized routing, note, done, or reopen transition.
An implementation runner, work-plan tracker, or completion-evidence consumer is outside this capability.

preconditions.statement: Reads require a selected current Todo database and any exact public ID or query required by the command.
Routing decisions require a pending current proposal plus a readable UTF-8 authorization source; rejection also requires a nonblank reason.

inputs.statement: Inputs are typed cN, rN, or tN identities, search text and documented filters or limits, note text, and exact decision source or rejection reason where applicable.
A model result, Nucleus completion, stale proposal, or untyped row number cannot serve as decision authorization.

outputs.statement: Read commands return exact concern, proposal, umbrella, direction, attachment, note, lifecycle, assessment, design, decision, staleness, or supersession projections selected by the command.
Writes return one durable provenance-bearing routing decision, immutable nN note, or idempotent open/done lifecycle result.

data_semantics.statement: cN, rN, tN, aN, dN, and nN denote different durable concepts; staleness is derived comparison data and never rewrites historical decisions.
Attachment does not revise direction, revision does not merge identities, unification retains superseded identities and history, and done does not assert external implementation.

identity_and_units.statement: Public typed IDs retain their prefix semantics; tN is the stable umbrella identity while its title and direction derive from append-only revisions.
This capability publishes no quantitative accounting or pricing unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: An exact show returns the selected durable record and its documented current or historical projection; list and search return open canonical umbrellas by default and include applicable history only with --all.
Routing acceptance atomically rechecks the complete frozen proposal basis against current Todo state before applying it.
Todo reads do not establish the freshness or completion of independently owned external work.

access.statement: The supported surface is the noninteractive current-user Todo CLI over its selected local SQLite database; deterministic reads and writes do not invoke Nucleus.
Direct SQLite writes, model-side accept or reject tools, and force-overrides for stale routing are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Routing acceptance revalidates and applies its action in one immediate transaction; rejection records a terminal reason without applying it.
Notes are append-only, done and reopen are idempotent, direction revisions preserve umbrella identity, and unification retains one canonical survivor plus superseded history.

operational_limits.statement: List and search are bounded by documented limits, all mutation commands target one explicit Todo identity or proposal, and no delete or stale-force interface is provided.
No query-latency, database-size, retention-horizon, or external-state freshness service-level objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 1 preserves typed public identities, append-only history, explicit provenance-bearing decisions, and the open/done umbrella lifecycle.
No public deprecation period or perpetual compatibility window is promised.

reliances.statement: These reads and deterministic Todo writes invoke no other product and create no runtime, data, authority, or readiness reliance outside the selected local Todo state.
